answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the plume schedule in the river ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the ferrous checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 143 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 5 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 36 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
